title: Heuristic region ranking and capacity-aware shedding playbook for multi-region routing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We need a predictable, tunable routing layer that balances latency SLOs, per-region capacity headroom, and customer affinity. Current steering is brittle under surges: regions either starve or we cause cross-region latency spikes when we fail over too aggressively. This ticket defines a heuristic scoring function + circuit-breaker and shedding playbook to improve availability without materially increasing tail latency for routed requests.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Keep global P99 inference latency within SLOs (target: <= 250ms for short sequences, <= 600ms for long sequences) for 99% of requests when any single region degrades.
- Avoid saturation of a single region by preferring capacity-aware routes when possible.
- Provide graceful degradation via service-class shedding rather than hard failures.
- Make routing policy debuggable and observable (per-request region score breakdown, CB states, capacity credits).

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement region_score that combines latency, capacity headroom, error signal, and affinity with configurable weights.
- Circuit breaker states per region exposed in /routing/status and used by decision engine.
- Shedding policy that reduces non-essential features or token budgets for low-tier requests when global capacity drops below threshold.
- Automated AB experiment shows 30% reduction in cross-region rebalances during high surge windows and maintains SLO compliance for P95/P99 in canary traffic.

Design summary (heuristic):
- Compute per-region signals every 1s bucket: 1) EWMA latency (50ms EWMA alpha=0.2), 2) p99 latency window (1m), 3) capacity_headroom = (usable_slots - inflight_estimated) / usable_slots, 4) error_rate (30s window), 5) affinity_score (customer pin/geo).
- Region score function (normalized 0..100):
  region_score = w_affinity * affinity_score + w_lat * (1 - norm_latency) + w_cap * norm_headroom + w_err * (1 - norm_error)
  where weights are configurable per-customer tier. Default weights: w_affinity=0.15, w_lat=0.45, w_cap=0.30, w_err=0.10.
- Normalization: use rolling min/max with clamp to reduce outlier influence; apply logistic transform to latency to penalize tail growth.

Circuit breaker rules (region-level):
- Enter OPEN if any of:
  - p99_latency(region) > p99_slo * 1.5 for 2 consecutive 1m windows
  - error_rate(region) > 5% for 60s
  - capacity_headroom < 10% for 30s
- OPEN -> HALF_OPEN after cool_down = 60s * backoff_factor (backoff_factor doubles each OPEN)
- On HALF_OPEN attempt small percentage of traffic (2-5%) with strict timeouts; if healthy, close; otherwise re-open with increased backoff.

Capacity-aware shedding strategy:
- Priority classes: tier_enterprise, tier_standard, tier_free.
- When cluster-wide usable_headroom < 15% start staged shedding:
  1) reduce max_tokens_per_call by 30% for tier_free for requests that are not flagged "guaranteed_quota"
  2) degrade optional tool-calls/function-calls: convert to async batch path for non-critical calls
  3) if headroom < 5% escalate to blocking requests for tier_free with 429 + retry-after and route essential requests to dedicated spare pool (if configured)
- Shedding decisions must be logged as event with cause code (HEADROOM_LOW / REGION_CB_OPEN / GLOBAL_OVERLOAD) and attach region_score snapshot.

Routing fallback policy:
- Route selection picks highest region_score among regions that are CLOSED or HALF_OPEN (probabilistic acceptance on HALF_OPEN).
- If selected region rejects due to sudden overload, request is re-scored and retried up to N=2 times with exponential backoff starting at 50ms.
- If all regions exhausted, use degrade_fallback: return structured response with partial result + hint to retry or switch to async.

Observability and telemetry:
- Add per-request metadata fields: chosen_region, candidate_region_scores (top-3), route_attempts, cb_state_changes. These are included in trace spans and token-level cost events.
- Dashboards: steering_latency (p50/p95/p99 per-region), capacity_headroom heatmap, CB_state transitions histogram, shedding events over time.
- Alerting: page when region's CB opens and 3xx/4xx/5xx error rate increases > 1% over baseline for 5 minutes.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement scoring and CB in decision engine, enabled for 1% of traffic for internal customers only. Observe 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (expanded): enable for 10% external traffic with AB experiment comparing SLOs and cross-region churn.
- Phase 3 (global): full rollout with toggle per-customer and per-route.

Testing and validation:
- Synthetic chaos tests: region p99 spike, simulated sudden capacity drop, regional network partition. Confirm routing stabilizes and shedding triggers.
- Load tests: ramp to 2x baseline QPS, confirm headroom metrics and shedding thresholds behave as designed.
- Perf targets: end-to-end failover added latency < 150ms median for retried requests.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Weight defaults vs per-customer tuning: start conservative defaults and expose simple sliders in Console; advanced customers can supply custom weight profile.
- How aggressive to shed optional features vs token budget: prefer shedding features first for UX preservation.
- Whether to persist backoff state across controller restarts: prototype will keep in-memory, long-term plan is durable state in Redis for cluster continuity.

updates: 2026-02-12 - Ticket created by Asha Patel: initial problem statement and high-level design.

2026-02-25 - Prototype landed (internal feature branch): scoring calculation integrated into decision engine, basic /routing/status endpoint added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/694. Preliminary tests show reduced cross-region churn in synthetic spikes.

2026-03-03 - Design review with PM (Sofia Martinez) and SRE: increased default weight for capacity to 0.30 and reduced affinity weight. PM requested opt-out flag for enterprise customers. Added to spec.

2026-03-08 - Canary started (1% internal traffic) using routing-2026.03 build. Observability: no CB opens in first 48h. Noted noisy headroom metric due to scheduler estimation; filed follow-up ENG-744445 to tighten headroom estimator.
2026-03-10 - Updated scoring normalization to clamp extremes and switched logistic transform implementation to reduce sensitivity to a single outlier region. Planning AB for 10% expansion next week.
